dek.text: Cameras on Dallas sanitation trucks scanned {{number:c46}} properties. A city memo counts {{number:c47}} citations, issued only after an in-person inspection.

introduction.text: [Dallas put cameras made by City Detect on its bulk trash trucks](c57), [and they scan homes and buildings for potential code violations](c49). [The city's own briefing to its Finance Committee says the cameras face sideways and capture images from the public right of way](c5).

[A city memo dated {{date:c45}}](c45) [says the cameras scanned {{number:c46}} properties](c46). [It counts {{number:c47}} citations at {{number:c47:1}} properties](c47). A flagged image is a possible problem, not a violation, and the steps between the two decide who gets a visit.

sections.heading: How a flag becomes a citation

paragraphs.text: [The software assigns blight scores that help Code Compliance decide which properties to review first](c51). [The memo says the citations came after camera detections were reviewed and confirmed by code officers](c50), [and that a citation is issued only after a code officer inspects the property in person and notifies the owner](c47).

[The city's December briefing said the system is neither a staff replacement nor automated ticketing](c12) [and that a person stays in the loop](c13). [It said faces and license plates are blurred](c6).

[The city sent courtesy notices to approximately {{number:c53}} property owners after potential violations were detected](c53). [City officials say the notices are not citations or formal warnings and require no action, though they warn that a continuing violation could bring enforcement](c54). [Code Compliance also opened about {{number:c52}} cases where officials believe an in-person inspection should come soon](c52).
Those counts measure different things, and they are not a step by step tally from detection to citation.

[By the city manager's memo, {{number:c55}} of the citations were issued in Council Districts {{number:c55:2}}, {{number:c55:3}} and {{number:c55:4}} in southern Dallas](c55). [Council member Chad West has raised concerns that the technology could put a disproportionate financial burden on neighborhoods with fewer resources](c59).

[The three-year contract is estimated at {{money:c9}}, subject to annual City Council appropriations](c9). [It costs {{money:c10}} a year](c10), [and the city may end it on {{number:c11}} days' written notice](c11). [West proposed removing the program's funding and withdrew the request after the city manager's office agreed to brief the council](c56).
